producer_report.summary: Each card on decisions.html now leads with a plain yes/no question ('Go ahead with this: <title>?'). Next come an 'If yes' line, an 'If no' line, a cost and risk line, and a bold 'Recommend yes:' or 'Recommend no:' line with its reason. The rung, raising role, source, evidence, record id and GitHub record link sit in a collapsed `<details>` element below. The visible text no longer names rungs, roles or record kinds. The cost line and the recommendation are templates chosen from the rung and the raising role's recorded limit. The word cap and Brief::check now apply to the visible lines. The recommendation must start with 'Recommend yes:' or 'Recommend no:' and give a reason. I rewrote the page lede and the module docs. I updated owner-style.md and CHANGELOG.md, and added a small CSS rule in site.rs for the details element. New tests check the line order against the first path or record id, the collapsed details, and the owner-style rules across a sample page of three cards.

checks_run.note: 65 unit tests plus ci_shards, fingerprint, policy (boundary scan), site_page, spec and walltime all passed
applied formatting; the --check form was not run

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask`: a new test renders a card (Brief::html) from a sample WorkItem proposal and asserts the byte offsets of the question (ending in '?'), the 'If yes' line, the 'If no' line, the cost/risk line and the recommendation line are all smaller than the offset of the first evidence path, record id or record link.
criteria_check.evidence: Test the_question_yes_no_cost_and_recommendation_come_before_any_path_or_record_id passes. It takes the minimum byte offset of the evidence path, job id, record path and href in Brief::html output. It asserts each of the five lines sits before that offset, and in order.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask`: a test asserts the evidence list, record id and GitHub record link sit inside a collapsed `<details>` element (no `open` attribute) in the card HTML, and nothing visible outside it contains a path or record id.
criteria_check.evidence: Test evidence_record_id_and_link_sit_in_a_collapsed_details_element passes. It checks there is one plain `<details>` with no `open`, that evidence, href and record path are inside it, and that the visible text (details removed, tags stripped) has no evidence, href, `records/`, `.md`, record id, job id or commit id.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask`: a test renders a sample page of several cards and checks owner-style rules mechanically: each card's visible words are within MAX_WORDS, the visible text contains none of the banned jargon (rung names, role names, 'work item', 'proposal', 'blind spot', 'job', 'commit', 'path'), and each card has exactly one question.
criteria_check.evidence: Test a_sample_page_of_cards_follows_the_owner_style_rules passes. For three cards it checks the visible word count against MAX_WORDS, exactly one '?', and whole-word absence of the banned jargon, rung names and role names. It also checks the recommendations come out [yes, no, no].

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask`: the recommendation line states Recommend yes or Recommend no with a one-line reason, and a card without a recommendation is still refused by Brief::check.
criteria_check.evidence: Tests the_recommendation_follows_the_raising_roles_recorded_limit and a_brief_over_the_word_limit_or_without_a_recommendation_is_refused pass. The first asserts the exact `Recommend yes: ...` and `Recommend no: ...` lines. The second shows check refuses an empty line, `Recommendation:`, `Recommend yes:` with no reason, and `Do it.`, and accepts `Recommend no: too costly.`.

criteria_check.criterion: The diff touches no file under records/, athena.toml, defaults.toml or .github/workflows, and adds no record or data file under crates/.
criteria_check.evidence: Edited files are xtask/src/decisions.rs, xtask/src/site.rs (CSS), docs/conventions/owner-style.md and CHANGELOG.md only.

open_issues: Cost and risk are estimates fixed by rung (high, medium or low). That is not data from the record, and the owner may want finer wording.

A proposal from a role at or below its limit now gets 'Recommend yes'; one above its limit, or from an unrecorded role, gets 'Recommend no'. This is my reading of the old 'decide yourself' rule and needs the owner's judgement.
The 'audience role rates a sample page' part of the request is covered only by mechanical tests. No separate reader rated the page.
mistakes: My first Edit of the HTML-writing code dropped the backslashes in the string and failed; I redid it with the backslashes.
The first CHANGELOG edit failed because several `### Added` headings matched; I redid it with the `## [Unreleased]` heading as context.
learnings: The Brief word cap and Brief::check now cover only the visible lines; the collapsed details are not counted.
A proposal record has no yes/no, cost or risk field, so those lines are templates filled from the title and rung.
The policy boundary scan runs as part of cargo test -p xtask.
